newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil eyes 17-21 mln bag 1997-98 coffee harvest.
newsitem.headline: Brazil eyes 17-21 mln bag 1997-98 coffee harvest.

text.p: Brazil's 1997-98 coffee harvest is forecast at between 17 million and 21 million 60-kg bags, said Jose Braz Matielo, coordinator for Procafe, an arm of of Brazil's Ministry of Agriculture.
"There has been a slowdown in planting in 1996-97 compared to 1995-96," Braz Matielo told a coffee conference. "There will be less planting due to lower prices."
A decline in rainfall combined with higher temperatures and a biannual cyclical downturn in production would also contribute to the drop in the 1997-98 harvest, he said.

In Minas Gerais state, responsible for about 50 percent of Brazil's total coffee crop, production would be 5 million to 7 million bags below 1996-97 levels, he said. Originally, the government thought the state's 1997-98 output would be just 3 million to 5 million bags lower than 1996-97.
In most key producing states production was also set to drop sharply, Braz Matielo said.
